title: Cyrus and the Songbook
premise: August Ashgrove inherited a failing vineyard and a decade of unsigned letters from a stranger who knew her better than anyone — letters she answered under a false name, falling in love with a voice. When Cyrus Vale, the quiet new neighbor, arrives with a songbook full of her own words set to music, August realizes he is the letter-writer: an ex-convict rebuilding his life after taking the fall for a crime committed by the man who now holds the lien on her vineyard. As August fights to expose the truth before the property is seized, she must choose between the loyalty of the town that condemned Cyrus and the truth that could free them both; in the end, she speaks the rehearsed sentence at the county hearing — 'I believe him' — saving the vineyard not with money but with testimony, and choosing a love built on truth over the safe silence she trained herself into.
about_author: Astrid Reyes is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent years covering courtrooms in wine country before turning to fiction. She writes love stories about people who learn that honesty is a kind of courage.

chapters.title: The Weight of Untended Vines
chapters.summary: August's POV. Three years after inheriting Ashgrove Vineyard buried in debt, August runs the estate on discipline and denial, rereading the anonymous letters she's exchanged for a decade with someone who signs only 'C.' The bank's final notice arrives. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Guitar Case
chapters.summary: August's POV. Cyrus Vale rents the neighboring cottage, courteous and guarded, helping when a storm breaks her irrigation lines. He hums melodies she almost recognizes. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth cracking her armor.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Signed
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashbacks reveal how he began writing to a stranger from prison, and why he moved to Ashgrove knowing whose land bordered his cottage. He recognizes August instantly; she doesn't know his face. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by guilt.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: August's POV. She discovers Cyrus's songbook left open on his porch — her own sentences, verbatim, set to music. Confrontation turns raw as he admits he is 'C,' and confesses he served ten years for a crime he didn't commit, one tied to the man foreclosing on her vineyard. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition colliding.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The town still brands Cyrus guilty; August's oldest friend warns her away from him. Meanwhile Cyrus names the true culprit: Marcus Hale, the investor holding her lien, whose crime sent Cyrus to prison. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against evidence.

chapters.title: Harvest Before the Storm
chapters.summary: August's POV. With foreclosure weeks away, August and Cyrus bring in the harvest together, and intimacy grows between rows of grapes. She rehearses the sentence she's never dared say aloud. Emotional beat: tenderness under a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Hale offers to forgive August's debt if Cyrus leaves town and stops talking. Cyrus nearly accepts to protect her; August finds the signed offer and refuses it for both of them. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: Evidence in the Cellar
chapters.summary: August's POV. Digging through her father's old records, August finds proof her late father knew of Hale's guilt — and stayed silent, trading his silence for the loan that doomed the vineyard. Emotional beat: grief for a father's cowardice, fury turned to purpose.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the county hearing on the foreclosure and Cyrus's petition to reopen his case, Hale's lawyer dismantles their credibility until August takes the stand and says the rehearsed sentence: 'I believe him.' Her testimony, the records, and the songbook's dated lyrics break Hale's alibi. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage.

chapters.title: First Verse, Sung Whole
chapters.summary: August's POV. Hale is indicted, the debt collapses, and Cyrus's conviction is vacated. On the porch where she found the songbook, Cyrus sings her letter back to her, and she answers with her own verse at last. Emotional beat: love chosen freely, identity made whole.
